2770 physical TOPDON 96x96 thermometry acceptance

This is an executable human procedure for a reserved Linux board. Generation
does not contact a board. No existing committed thermal frame is claimed to be
a physical recording. Every case starts not_run. An offline replay can prove
decoder behavior for supplied bytes; physical provenance and reference accuracy
still require a human review. Never commit raw camera files, images or videos.

Target and measurement contract

Use the source-supported USB device 2bdf:0102, bcdDevice 0409. Pin its serial,
physical USB port, stable camera ID, board serial, OS/kernel and installed Agent
binary hash. Save the original lsusb -v and udevadm output, not just a label
typed into JSON. The usb_descriptor inventory file is a transcription with
idVendor/idProduct/bcdDevice/serial/port fields; retain its original console
output beside it. If the USB device has no serial descriptor, record the literal
not-reported in both inventory and transcription; retain a photographed bench
asset label and the fixed USB port as the physical-unit identity. Never invent
a USB serial. If firmware cannot be read independently, state that only
the USB-reported revision is known. Do not invent a firmware version.

The camera list must declare topdon-tc001-hik-v1, capture_width 96 and
capture_height 200. The raw message has YUYV layout, 192 bytes per line and
38400 bytes per frame. Only rows 0..95 are the 96x96 sensor plane. Row 97 holds
the geometry header; rows 100..195 are the preview; row 196 holds the summary.
The summary temperature code is not a raw sensor pixel. Applying code/64-50 to
the sensor plane is wrong. Calibration is not established by the camera name,
an encoded preview, a synthetic fixture or matching two copies of the decoder.

Before capture, document an independent temperature reference. Use an in-date
calibrated blackbody target or an appropriate calibrated contact probe with a
stable high-emissivity target whose surface temperature is independently known.
Record instrument serial, calibration certificate/hash, emissivity, distance,
focus, ambient/reflected temperature, equilibration time and combined uncertainty.
Predeclare the acceptance tolerance and safe cool/warm target temperatures.
An uncalibrated thermometer, human skin temperature estimate or the TOPDON's own
display is not an independent reference. If no suitable reference is available,
capture may still document protocol/geometry but Celsius accuracy remains pending.
Choose a threshold between the safe cool and warm references. Do not heat to the
default 80C just to test an alert. Put the selected finite threshold in inventory.

Prepare without device operations

1. Generate the plan from captured inventory/provenance files:
     python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/topdon-physical-rehearsal.py INVENTORY_JSON NEW_DIRECTORY
   Its schema is in the generator docstring. The generated app is an exact copy
   of ThermalNotify source with a unique app ID, admin entitlement only and
   monitor-only environment. No Cloud notifications are sent or requested.
   Generation does not build or deploy the app. Keep the original example intact.

2. From the pinned repository checkout, build the bounded capture helper:
     @BUILD@
   Save source SHA, Go version, command output and sha256sum of the result. The
   helper only calls ListVideoDevices and StreamVideo on an explicitly supplied
   local admin Unix socket. It never opens video nodes or changes capture size.
   Copy it and the plan to a fresh private directory on the reserved board using
   the bench's authorized transport. Recheck its hash on the board. Do not change
   admin-socket permissions to make the test work. Use the already authorized
   bench account; absence of local access is a prerequisite, not a reason to
   substitute a fake server or contact Cloud.

3. Verify the installed Agent executable through /proc/<actual-main-pid>/exe,
   its hash, service start time and boot ID. Save the exact camera list command
   below, lsusb -v -d 2bdf:0102 and:
     udevadm info --query=all --name="$OBSERVED_CAMERA_NODE"
     v4l2-ctl --device="$OBSERVED_CAMERA_NODE" --all --list-formats-ext
   Match camera stable ID to this node and serial/port. Save clock synchronization
   state, UTC time and reference-instrument time offset. The replay checks Agent
   frame UTC against capture-helper receipt UTC; it never rewrites old timestamps
   to now. Close only bench-owned viewers before starting so the default physical
   96x200 mode is selected. A 256x392 or picture-only stream cannot cover 2770.

Collect the real reusable frame sequence

4. Observe the actual local Agent admin socket from its service/runtime state.
   The current host default is /var/lib/wendy/agent-control/agent.sock, and an
   admin-entitled app receives /run/wendy/agent/agent.sock. Select the real socket,
   not a guessed network endpoint. On the board, in the private directory:
     @CAPTURE@ --socket "$OBSERVED_AGENT_SOCKET" --output "$NEW_RECORDING_DIRECTORY"
   This is an explicit hardware operation. It stops at 60 seconds or 1600 frames,
   whichever happens first, and cancellation closes its own RPC. It writes only
   a NEW output directory, at most about 83 MB. Start it only when ready to follow
   the physical sequence. The capture's status 'captured' only means transport
   collection completed; physical_acceptance still requires review.

5. During that minute, issue a fresh written run nonce and record a UTC timeline.
   First show the stable cool target. Move the independently measured warmer
   target through left, center and right parts of the 96x96 field, with a cool
   background and no hotter object elsewhere. Hold each position long enough to
   see several distinct summary updates. Then remove it, wait for the cool
   reading, and introduce it again. Log reference temperatures and target pixel
   regions independently of the decoded coordinates. Save the target arrangement
   and instrument display as external review assets, with acquisition times.
   Do not use a rendered palette as the temperature reference. Changing raw sensor
   values alone does not prove that the summary changed or its location is valid.

6. Retain camera.json, manifest.json and every frame-*.json without editing them.
   Each frame file contains the full Agent protobuf JSON, including original raw
   bytes in base64, thermal-plane description and timestamp. Manifest entries
   contain receipt timestamps, file hashes and raw-payload hashes. Copy the whole
   directory to the workstation and verify hashes before and after transfer.
   A missing/truncated sequence, changed layout, early camera error or no fresh
   summary must remain incomplete. Keep the initial cached summary too; do not
   discard it to make freshness tests pass.

Independent byte and reference inspection

7. For at least three post-startup changed summaries at distinct target positions,
   inspect the original bytes without calling Wendy's decoder. This command
   reads a captured frame JSON and prints unsigned little-endian metadata words:
     python3 inspect-frame.py "$FRAME_JSON"
   Header words 0/1 must be ccdd/aabb; 32-bit little-endian dimensions at header
   offsets 8 and 12 must both be 96. Summary words 0/1 must be ffff/eeee. Word 2
   is maximum code and word 5 minimum code; both must be between 1 and 65534 with
   maximum >= minimum. Words 3/4 and 6/7 are normalized coordinates in 0..1000.
   Independently transcribe max Celsius = word2 / 64 - 50 and compare to the
   simultaneous external reference within the PREDECLARED uncertainty. Convert
   max coordinates by floor((normalized * 95 + 500)/1000); compare to the target
   region recorded before looking at decoded coordinates. Save the arithmetic,
   raw words, instrument observations and chosen frame indices.

8. Copy reference.template.json to the recording directory as reference.json.
   Fill observer, independent instrument serial and the calibration-record hash.
   Add at least three samples using this schema, with actual observed values:
     {"frame": INDEX, "expected_max_celsius": MANUAL_METADATA_RESULT,
      "reference_celsius": INDEPENDENT_INSTRUMENT_READING,
      "tolerance_celsius": PREDECLARED_UNCERTAINTY,
      "x_min": LEFT, "x_max": RIGHT, "y_min": TOP, "y_max": BOTTOM}
   The regions are inclusive sensor coordinates 0..95, not 96x200 capture rows.
   Never fill an expected value from ThermalNotify's output merely to pass replay.
   Preserve the immutable capture separately from this reviewed annotation file.

Replay with the actual ThermalNotify implementation

9. On a macOS 15+ workstation with the package's Swift toolchain, use a private
   checkout of the exact candidate. Copy RecordedTopdonTests.swift
   into its Examples/ThermalNotify/Tests/ThermalNotifyTests directory. It is a
   test template outside the normal package, so no physical file is required by
   ordinary CI. Set TOPDON_RECORDING to the absolute reviewed recording path:
     TOPDON_RECORDING="$RECORDING" swift test --package-path "$PRIVATE_CHECKOUT/Examples/ThermalNotify" --filter recordedTopdonReplay
   Save full compiler/test output, Package.resolved and source SHA. Do not copy
   recordings into the repository. The test verifies file/raw hashes, original
   timestamps, real decoder geometry/Celsius, external reference/regions, startup
   suppression and at least one changed fresh summary. It runs actual AlertState
   at the measured threshold and one metadata count below it: equal does not
   trigger, above triggers once, sustained heat does not retrigger, cool rearms.

   The stale timestamp, frozen summary with advancing receipt/video time, corrupt
   header/trailer and truncated-payload cases are explicitly DERIVED controls.
   They never overwrite a recorded frame. These controls establish software
   rejection using real captured bytes; they do not claim the camera itself was
   made to freeze or emit corrupt metadata. Save a failing historical control
   by running the same test in another private checkout with only ThermalReading's
   96x200 layout acceptance removed. Require failure at the supported-layout
   assertion, then rerun the unmodified candidate. A compiler error is not proof.

Observe the physical source through the running monitor

10. From @OUTPUT@/app, run the generated bounded attached command below. The app
    ID is @APP_ID@. Its build can be prepared first with the same CLI's `build`
    command and explicit device selector. Do not change the example's live app.
    The command is bounded to 300 seconds including startup; if building consumes
    the interval, this is an incomplete run. Attached cancellation requests only
    this owned app to stop. Confirm actual container state and logs separately.
    Require startup logs naming the exact stable ID, configured threshold and
    'Monitor-only mode: no Cloud notifications will be sent.'

11. Repeat the safe cool/warm/cool/warm physical target sequence and independent
    reference log. Require startup waiting until the HIK summary changes, a valid
    Celsius log with camera-reported provenance, one 'MONITOR ONLY' event above
    the chosen threshold, no duplicate during sustained warmth, and a second
    event only after a valid cool measurement rearms it. Allow the global 10-second
    send spacing. Do not infer absence from a short log tail; retain the entire
    attached run and UTC sequence. No Cloud delivery or notification acceptance
    is part of this procedure. A reference tolerance spanning the threshold is
    inconclusive; use safe setpoints clearly on either side.

Cleanup and fixture custody

12. Let the bounded helper and attached CLI finish. Use the exact generated apps
    command to verify the unique app is stopped. If necessary run stop_owned_app
    for that exact app ID and verify again; do not stop an existing ThermalNotify
    deployment. Verify helper RPC/camera capture children are gone and the camera
    can be reopened normally. Restore only bench-owned device order/settings from
    the recovery record. Preserve uncertain cleanup evidence for the bench owner.

13. Preserve an access-controlled archive of the ORIGINAL recording plus hashes,
    source/binary pins, USB/kernel/firmware provenance, instrument calibration,
    nonce/timeline, reviewed reference.json, replay normal/control logs and live
    monitor logs. Save the archive URL and SHA256 in the audit evidence. A later
    approved fixture may store raw bytes outside Git and fetch by pinned hash;
    do not commit frames or images to satisfy reuse. An independent reviewer must
    accept provenance, uncertainty, geometry, freshness, threshold and cleanup
    separately. Missing hardware or reference evidence stays pending. Never turn
    a synthetic local validation run into a physical acceptance result.
